items.question: Should cars be banned from city centres?

people.name: Priya
people.text: I was sure a ban would ruin my bakery, because many of my customers drive in from the suburbs. Then our high street was closed to traffic for a trial month, and my takings actually rose: people lingered, sat outside and bought more than before. I'm still uneasy about a permanent rule, though. Some of my older customers can't walk far and need somewhere to be dropped off right by the door. If the council provides that, I would support a ban without any hesitation at all.

people.name: Carlos
people.text: A complete ban is unrealistic. Plenty of people work shifts that end at midnight, when the buses have stopped running, and they can't cycle home safely along dark roads. A fairer approach is to charge drivers a daily fee, with discounts for residents. That reduces traffic without punishing those who have no other way of getting around. I would also rather see the money from the charge spent on frequent, cheap buses than on prettier pavements and flower beds. Otherwise the policy will look like a punishment for ordinary workers.

people.name: Hannah
people.text: I live above a main road, and my daughter's asthma gets much worse on days when the air is thick with exhaust fumes. So for me this is about health, not convenience, and I don't care much if some people complain about parking. But I accept that bans only work if public transport is dependable. Where I live, the tram breaks down almost every week, and that makes me hesitate to ask other people to leave their cars at home.

people.name: Kwame
people.text: I drive a delivery van, so a ban would hit my job directly. Yet I'm not against limits. Unloading during the busiest hours is chaos, and I would happily start before eight in the morning if I were allowed to. What annoys me is the idea that all drivers are the same. Most of us are working, not sightseeing. Give businesses a proper permit and I will accept tough restrictions on private cars without complaining. Treat us as professionals and we will cooperate.

statements.text: Poor air quality affects the speaker's own family.

explanation.en: Hannah says her daughter's asthma gets worse when the air is thick with exhaust fumes.
explanation.es: Hannah dice que el asma de su hija empeora cuando el aire está cargado de humos.

statements.text: A short experiment proved the speaker's financial fears wrong.

explanation.en: Priya feared the ban would ruin her bakery, but during the trial month her takings rose.
explanation.es: Priya temía que la prohibición arruinara su panadería, pero durante el mes de prueba sus ingresos subieron.

statements.text: Making motorists pay is a better solution than forbidding them to enter.

explanation.en: Carlos calls a complete ban unrealistic and prefers to charge drivers a daily fee.
explanation.es: Carlos dice que una prohibición total no es realista y prefiere cobrar a los conductores una tarifa diaria.

statements.text: The speaker would accept restrictions if deliveries could be made at quieter times.

explanation.en: Kwame would happily start before eight in the morning and will accept restrictions if businesses get a permit.
explanation.es: Kwame empezaría gustosamente antes de las ocho y aceptaría restricciones si las empresas tuvieran un permiso.

statements.text: Customers with limited mobility must still be able to get close to the shops.

explanation.en: Priya says older customers who can't walk far need somewhere to be dropped off by the door.
explanation.es: Priya dice que los clientes mayores que no pueden caminar mucho necesitan un sitio donde los dejen junto a la puerta.

statements.text: People who finish work very late may have no safe alternative to driving.

explanation.en: Carlos mentions shifts that end at midnight, when the buses have stopped and cycling home is unsafe.
explanation.es: Carlos menciona turnos que acaban a medianoche, cuando ya no hay autobuses y volver en bici no es seguro.

statements.text: The speaker is reluctant to make demands on other people because local transport lets them down.

explanation.en: Hannah says the tram breaks down almost every week, so she hesitates to ask others to leave their cars at home.
explanation.es: Hannah dice que el tranvía se avería casi cada semana, así que duda en pedir a otros que dejen el coche en casa.
